text:
maria: Heads-up — since the kernel-selector tweak yesterday we're seeing a ~9% drop in prefix cache hit rate on prod cohorts.
sam: Can you paste the cohort and timeframe? is this overall or just long-context workloads?
maria: Observed across mixed workloads but highest on 1024+ seqs. Window 03:00-06:00 UTC, cohort=stable-serving-1.
taylor: I pulled a small profile. Kernel selector picks smaller-kernel path more often now -> more KV cache evictions during batch boundary reshuffle.
anya: Interesting, did the selector change alter batching alignments? we've seen evictions when batch boundaries shift.
maria: Exactly. The selector tries to favor lower-latency kernels for short sequences which caused batch composition variance. That led to more partial K/V cache mismatches.
nate: From logs I see a lot of misses where probe key differs by tokenizer variant: tokenization v2 vs v2.1 produced different whitespace tokens for system prompt.
maria: Oof. So two things: kernel routing changed batching, and tokenizer drift changed canonical keying. Both multiply.
sam: Repro plan: 1) run isolated trace with kernel-selector off, 2) replay requests with pinned tokenizer v2.1, 3) compare hit curves.
anya: I made a quick diff of keys. Example:
```
key_before: "sys:\nYou are an assistant.\nUser: hi"
key_after:  "sys:\nYou are an assistant. \nUser: hi"
```
Notice extra space after sentence in v2.1 -> different canonicalized prefix hash.
taylor: Small normalization fix (trim multi-space, normalize quotes) would collapse a lot of these diffs but we need to be careful with function/toolcall arg ordering — we mustn't normalize semantics away.
maria: Agreed. Proposal: implement a safe-normalizer that handles whitespace and non-semantic punctuation, but preserves tool signatures and arg ordering. Also pin tokenizer to v2.1 at serving layer for next 24h to quantify impact.
devops-bot: Deploy request queued: pin-tokenizer=v2.1 to rollout group stable-serving-1. CI checks passed.
nate: Also see that warmup job backfill was disabled during last deploy; restoring backfill reduces cold misses by ~6% in canary test.
sam: Action items: (A) rollback kernel-selector to previous routing for 2h experiment OR add a batching-stability flag, (B) pin tokenizer v2.1 for affected groups, (C) push safe-normalizer prototype behind feature flag, (D) re-enable warmup backfill and monitor hit-rate.
anya: I'll own (C) and add unit tests for toolcall-preservation. taylor can you sketch the normalizer rules?
taylor: Will do. Draft rules: collapse >1 whitespace to single, normalize CR/LF to \n, trim spaces adjacent to punctuation except inside JSON/tool args, preserve key order for "tool" objects.
maria: Nate and I will run the A/B with/without kernel-selector and collect per-token latency + hit-rate + eviction counts. We'll post CSV to #eng-runtime when ready.
devops-bot: Canary rollout started for pin-tokenizer=v2.1 group stable-serving-1.
sam: If we see >5% relative hit-rate recovery, prioritize normalizer rollout; else plan deeper kernel-selector revert.
maria: Thanks. I'll open a short postmortem draft once we have numbers. For now: holding any large config changes until A/B completes. :thumbsup:
